meaning: The highest purpose of human life is a kind of devotion to the Supreme that has no selfish motive and is never interrupted. Only this fully satisfies the self.
sanskrit:
स वै पुंसां परो धर्मो यतो भक्तिरधोक्षजे ।
अहैतुक्यप्रतिहता ययात्मा सुप्रसीदति ॥ ६ ॥
translit:
sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo
yato bhaktir adhokṣaje
ahaituky apratihatā
yayātmā suprasīdati

meaning: Hearing and speaking about the Lord is purifying. The Lord, who is the well-wisher of those who turn to Him, sits in the heart and gradually clears away the inner impurities that disturb us.
sanskrit:
श‍ृण्वतां स्वकथाः कृष्णः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः ।
हृद्यन्तःस्थो ह्यभद्राणि विधुनोति सुहृत्सताम् ॥ १७ ॥
translit:
śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ
hṛdy antaḥ stho hy abhadrāṇi
vidhunoti suhṛt satām

meaning: When disturbing things in the heart are almost destroyed by regular hearing and service, steady, loving faith becomes firmly established, and the mind becomes calm.
sanskrit:
नष्टप्रायेष्वभद्रेषु नित्यं भागवतसेवया ।
भगवत्युत्तमश्लोके भक्तिर्भवति नैष्ठिकी ॥ १८ ॥
translit:
naṣṭa-prāyeṣv abhadreṣu
nityaṁ bhāgavata-sevayā
bhagavaty uttama-śloke
bhaktir bhavati naiṣṭhikī

meaning: With every sunrise and sunset a person's life gets shorter. The only time that is not wasted is time spent on meaningful, uplifting topics. This is a reminder to use each day with purpose.
sanskrit:
आयुर्हरति वै पुंसामुद्यन्नस्तं च यन्नसौ ।
तस्यर्ते यत्क्षणो नीत उत्तमश्लोकवार्तया ॥ १७ ॥
translit:
āyur harati vai puṁsām
udyann astaṁ ca yann asau
tasyarte yat-kṣaṇo nīta
uttama-śloka-vārtayā

meaning: In the company of sincere, caring people, talks about the Lord are pleasing to the heart and the ear. Listening to them with faith leads step by step to progress, comfort and joy.
sanskrit:
सतां प्रसङ्गान्मम वीर्यसंविदो
भवन्ति हृत्कर्णरसायनाः कथाः ।
तज्जोषणादाश्वपवर्गवर्त्मनि
श्रद्धा रतिर्भक्तिरनुक्रमिष्यति ॥ २५ ॥
translit:
satāṁ prasaṅgān mama vīrya-saṁvido
bhavanti hṛt-karṇa-rasāyanāḥ kathāḥ
taj-joṣaṇād āśv apavarga-vartmani
śraddhā ratir bhaktir anukramiṣyati

meaning: This verse lists nine simple practices of devotion: hearing, chanting, remembering, serving, worshiping, praying, working in a spirit of service, friendship, and surrendering oneself. It gives many easy ways to begin.
sanskrit:
श्रवणं कीर्तनं विष्णोः स्मरणं पादसेवनम् ।
अर्चनं वन्दनं दास्यं सख्यमात्मनिवेदनम् ॥ २३ ॥
translit:
śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ
smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam
arcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ
sakhyam ātma-nivedanam

meaning: A wise person should start practicing the path of devotion early in life, because human life is rare, temporary, and still very valuable. Do not postpone what matters most.
sanskrit:
कौमार आचरेत्प्राज्ञो धर्मान्भागवतानिह ।
दुर्लभं मानुषं जन्म तदप्यध्रुवमर्थदम् ॥ १ ॥
translit:
kaumāra ācaret prājño
dharmān bhāgavatān iha
durlabhaṁ mānuṣaṁ janma
tad apy adhruvam arthadam

meaning: A person who patiently accepts the difficulties of life as the result of their own past actions, sees them as a form of the Lord's mercy, and keeps offering their heart, words and body in prayer, is ready for freedom.
sanskrit:
तत्तेऽनुकम्पां सुसमीक्षमाणो
भुञ्जान एवात्मकृतं विपाकम् ।
हृद्वाग्वपुर्भिर्विदधन्नमस्ते
जीवेत यो मुक्तिपदे स दायभाक् ॥ ८ ॥
translit:
tat te ’nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇo
bhuñjāna evātma-kṛtaṁ vipākam
hṛd-vāg-vapurbhir vidadhan namas te
jīveta yo mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk

meaning: For those who take shelter of the Lord, the vast ocean of worldly troubles becomes as small as the water in a calf's hoofprint. For them, there is a place where danger does not exist at every step.
sanskrit:
समाश्रिता ये पदपल्लवप्लवं
महत्पदं पुण्ययशो मुरारेः ।
भवाम्बुधिर्वत्सपदं परं पदं
पदं पदं यद् विपदां न तेषाम् ॥ ५८ ॥
translit:
samāśritā ye pada-pallava-plavaṁ
mahat-padaṁ puṇya-yaśo murāreḥ
bhavāmbudhir vatsa-padaṁ paraṁ padaṁ
padaṁ padaṁ yad vipadāṁ na teṣām

meaning: Fear comes from being absorbed in things that are not our real identity and from forgetting who we really are. A wise person overcomes fear by turning to the Lord with firm faith.
sanskrit:
भयं द्वितीयाभिनिवेशतः स्या-
दीशादपेतस्य विपर्ययोऽस्मृतिः ।
तन्माययातो बुध आभजेत्तं
भक्त्यैकयेशं गुरुदेवतात्मा ॥ ३७ ॥
translit:
bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād
īśād apetasya viparyayo ’smṛtiḥ
tan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ
bhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devatātmā

meaning: In the story of Pingala, we learn that endless expectation and hope in other people is a great source of suffering, while letting go of that dependence brings the greatest peace. Once she gave up her hopes, she slept peacefully.
sanskrit:
आशा हि परमं दुःखं नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् ।
यथा सञ्छिद्य कान्ताशां सुखं सुष्वाप पिङ्गला ॥ ४४ ॥
translit:
āśā hi paramaṁ duḥkhaṁ
nairāśyaṁ paramaṁ sukham
yathā sañchidya kāntāśāṁ
sukhaṁ suṣvāpa piṅgalā

meaning: Even though this age is full of faults, it has one great quality: simply by chanting the holy names, a person can become free from attachment and attain the highest peace. It is a simple practice anyone can start today.
sanskrit:
कलेर्दोषनिधे राजन्नस्ति ह्येको महान् गुणः ।
कीर्तनादेव कृष्णस्य मुक्तसङ्गः परं व्रजेत् ॥ ५१ ॥
translit:
kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann
asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ
kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya
mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet

meaning: Queen Kunti prays that the hardships of life may come again and again, because in those hard times she remembered the Lord and saw Him. Difficult days can turn the heart toward what is truly dear.
sanskrit:
विपदः सन्तु ताः शश्वत्तत्र तत्र जगद्गुरो ।
भवतो दर्शनं यत्स्यादपुनर्भवदर्शनम् ॥ २५ ॥
translit:
vipadaḥ santu tāḥ śaśvat
tatra tatra jagad-guro
bhavato darśanaṁ yat syād
apunar bhava-darśanam

meaning: Even duties done perfectly are only tiring labor if they do not awaken some attraction to the message of the Lord. Work gets its deeper meaning from the heart's connection to the Lord.
sanskrit:
धर्मः स्वनुष्ठितः पुंसां विष्वक्सेनकथासु यः ।
नोत्पादयेद्यदि रतिं श्रम एव हि केवलम् ॥ ८ ॥
translit:
dharmaḥ svanuṣṭhitaḥ puṁsāṁ
viṣvaksena-kathāsu yaḥ
notpādayed yadi ratiṁ
śrama eva hi kevalam

meaning: The Lord is easy to approach for those who are weary of material life, but not for those puffed up by birth, wealth, education or beauty. Humility and tiredness of the ego open the door to peace.
translit:
janmaiśvarya-śruta-śrībhir
edhamāna-madaḥ pumān
naivārhaty abhidhātuṁ vai
tvām akiñcana-gocaram

meaning: A wise man in the Bhagavatam realizes that other people, his own body, the stars, his past deeds or time are not the real cause of his happiness and distress. The mind is the chief cause, so working with the mind brings relief.
sanskrit:
नायं जनो मे सुखदुःखहेतु-
र्न देवतात्मा ग्रहकर्मकालाः ।
मनः परं कारणमामनन्ति
संसारचक्रं परिवर्तयेद् यत् ॥ ४२ ॥
translit:
nāyaṁ jano me sukha-duḥkha-hetur
na devatātmā graha-karma-kālāḥ
manaḥ paraṁ kāraṇam āmananti
saṁsāra-cakraṁ parivartayed yat

meaning: In this age, the spiritual progress that earlier ages reached through long meditation, sacrifice or temple worship can be reached simply by chanting the Hare Krishna maha-mantra. It is a simple practice that anyone can begin today.
sanskrit:
कृते यद्ध्यायतो विष्णुं त्रेतायां यजतो मखैः ।
द्वापरे परिचर्यायां कलौ तद्धरिकीर्तनात् ॥ ५२ ॥
translit:
kṛte yad dhyāyato viṣṇuṁ
tretāyāṁ yajato makhaiḥ
dvāpare paricaryāyāṁ
kalau tad dhari-kīrtanāt
